title: Google rolls out new selfie video sign-in feature - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Straits Times - Google on July 23 launched a new selfie video sign-in feature, allowing users another option to log in to their accounts or recover them in case they are locked out due to forgotten passwords or lack of access to their preferred devices.

The Alphabet-owned company will allow users to set up verification by recording a brief video of themselves performing guided head movements that would capture multiple angles. Google will then save the recording and use it to authenticate the live videos that users upload during their sign-in attempts later on.

While the new feature could provide stronger protection against fraud and better account recovery options for users, especially in cases of lost or stolen devices, it could also raise some concerns around privacy and biometric data collection.

Google said that the selfie video is stored with the user’s consent, and the user has the option to delete it at any time in their Google account. The video will be used only for sign-in purposes, unless the user opts in to share it for additional use cases, the company said.

The company added it uses several security checks to detect impersonation attempts, including deepfakes, by comparing a new recording with the saved selfie video and requiring users to perform movements that confirm the video is live.

The feature is available to eligible Google Account users from July 23.

Companies currently rely on trusted devices, registered phone numbers, recovery contacts and two-factor authentication for account-recovery procedures. Biometric and facial recognition have long been a subject of privacy concerns.

title: Commotion in Parliament following warrant issued on MP Archchuna - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror)- A commotion flared up in Parliament after MP Ramanathan Archchuna claimed a warrant has been issued to arrest him for failing to attend courts today.

Leader of the Opposition Sajith Premadasa, who joined the crosstalk, said the MP should be allowed to speak in the House before taking action.

Deputy Speaker Rizvie Salih who responded said necessary action will be taken.

Deputy Minister Sunil Watagala said the MP should have informed the courts of his inability to attend courts today. An MP has to attend courts if he is an accused," he said.

title: US says it will use frozen Iranian assets to fund damage to ships as strikes continue - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - The US military says it has launched strikes on Iran for the 13th consecutive night, with Iranian state media saying four people have been killed and five injured.

It comes as US President Donald Trump said he would use Iranian assets held by the US to pay for "any damages to Ships, Cargo, or anything related thereto".

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi hit back at the threat that Trump called "fair and equitable", calling it an "incendiary precedent".

The latest strikes follow Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthis' claim to have attacked two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and growing concerns over increasing threats to global shipping caused oil prices to spike.

Iranian state media have reported explosions in key military and commercial sites in the south of the country including the port city Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island.

Trump had earlier promised "major military punishment" against Iran for attacks by the Houthis and Iran.

The US military says it carried out strikes to degrade Iran's ability to threaten civilian shipping in regional waters.

US Central Command (Centcom) said it had targeted "Iranian military command centers, drone storage facilities, communication networks, coastal surveillance sites and maritime capabilities".

But as the US pushes to regain control over the Strait of Hormuz, there's growing concern over new threats to shipping in the Red Sea from the Iran-backed Houthis.

That's helped push the price of crude oil back over $100 (GBP £52.31) a barrel - the highest level since May.

Reuters news agency reported that only one tanker went through the Strait on Thursday 24 July, citing ship-tracking data, which they said was the lowest level of transit since 7 May.

As tensions in the region continued, Trump said the damage to ships and cargo "will be paid for by Iranian Money that the United States has in its possession, and controls" and the amount could be "very substantial".

Iran's foreign minister responded to Trump, writing "Those who celebrate or profit from such funds should remember: once governments normalize confiscation, no one's assets are safe."

"Ensuing chaos will not be pretty or peaceful," Araghchi added.

Bahrain's Interior Ministry reported that its air sirens had been sounded and Iranian state media also said alarms had been activated in Jordan.

In June, the US and Iran agreed on a 14-point Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to halt military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, as well as to reach an agreement to end the war over the following 60 days.

But three weeks after it was signed, Trump declared the ceasefire "over" after Iranian attacks on ships in Hormuz, and US strikes in response.

Point 11 of the MoU detailed that the "United States of America undertakes to make fully available for use the frozen or restricted funds and assets of the Islamic Republic of Iran".

title: Birthday party shooting victim dies - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - A 39-year-old man who was critically injured in a shooting at a birthday party in Wattala has died after being admitted to the Colombo National Hospital, police said.

The shooting occurred at around 9:40 p.m. on July 23 inside a banquet hall in the Kadirana Palliyawatta area, where a birthday celebration was being held for the child of the brother of a man known by the alias "Mattakkuliye Kudu Roshan."

According to police, an unidentified gunman arrived at the venue in a motor vehicle, entered the reception hall wearing a helmet to conceal his identity, and allegedly opened fire with a pistol in an apparent attempt to target the attendee.

Police said the suspected target was not hit. Instead, the victim, who was standing nearby, sustained critical gunshot injuries. He was rushed to the Colombo National Hospital, where he later succumbed to his injuries.

The deceased has been identified as a 39-year-old resident of Borella.

Police allege that the intended target is a suspected drug trafficker and a suspect in a murder case.

Wattala Police are conducting further investigations to identify and arrest the suspect and to determine the motive behind the shooting.

title: Expired medicines: Are financial penalties alone an adequate deterrent? - Former envoy Kananathan - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Every day, thousands of Sri Lankans walk into hospitals and laboratories believing that every medicine they receive, every blood test conducted and every diagnosis made is governed by one principle: patient safety. They never imagine that expired chemicals could be used to produce their test results or that medicines past their expiry date could be dispensed for treatment. They trust that those entrusted with protecting life have already fulfilled that duty.

That is why the latest enforcement action by the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) should outrage every citizen.

The CAA yesterday initiated legal action against 23 private hospitals and medical laboratories after investigations reportedly uncovered expired chemicals allegedly being used in laboratory testing, expired medicines kept for patient care and sale, laboratory charges exceeding regulated prices, and expired chemicals stored alongside usable stock. Courts have imposed fines totalling nearly Rs. 5.8 million, while further prosecutions are expected against additional institutions.

These are not technical violations, clerical oversights or paperwork errors.

If expired chemicals are used in laboratory testing, the consequences can be catastrophic. A single inaccurate result can trigger a missed diagnosis, delayed treatment, unnecessary surgery, inappropriate medication or false reassurance that everything is normal. In healthcare, one wrong diagnosis is not simply an administrative lapse—it can decide whether a patient survives or dies.

Expired medicines raise even more disturbing concerns. Every patient has the right to expect medicines that meet accepted standards of safety, quality and effectiveness. No one seeking treatment should ever receive medicines that should have been destroyed instead of dispensed.

Perhaps even more alarming is the reported failure to separate expired chemicals from usable stock. If proven, this reflects not only gross negligence but a complete breakdown of inventory management, quality assurance and professional responsibility inside institutions entrusted with protecting human life.

The public deserves answers.

How long had these expired materials remained in circulation? Who authorised or ignored their continued storage? Were quality assurance systems functioning? Were audits manipulated or neglected? Were patients harmed? Have affected patients been identified? Have corrective measures been independently verified? Most importantly, who will be held personally accountable?

These questions extend far beyond the courtroom.

The fines imposed by the courts are substantial on paper. But for large private healthcare institutions generating significant revenue, financial penalties alone risk becoming nothing more than another operating expense. If institutions can simply pay fines and continue business as usual, the law has failed to protect the public. Patient safety demands consequences that cannot simply be written off.

A compromised medicine cannot restore lost health. A wrong diagnosis cannot reverse irreversible harm. Human lives cannot be compensated with fines.

This is precisely why regulators must use every legal power available whenever serious or repeated violations are established. Institutions found guilty should face suspension of operating licences, cancellation of licences for repeated offences, criminal prosecution of responsible directors and managers, disqualification from holding healthcare management positions, mandatory public disclosure of violations, and compensation for patients where harm has occurred. Accountability must reach the individuals responsible—not merely the corporate entity.

Equally important is restoring public confidence.

Sri Lanka’s healthcare professionals have earned enormous respect through decades of dedicated service. Thousands of doctors, nurses, laboratory scientists and pharmacists uphold the highest professional standards every day. Their integrity should never be tarnished by institutions that place profits, negligence or weak governance above patient safety. Strong enforcement protects patients while safeguarding the reputation of the overwhelming majority of healthcare professionals who faithfully follow the law.

The CAA deserves recognition for conducting islandwide inspections instead of waiting for tragedy to expose systemic failures. Prevention remains the strongest form of public protection.

But enforcement must not end with fines, headlines and forgotten court cases.

Expired medicines and chemicals have absolutely no place in any hospital, laboratory or pharmacy. If investigations confirm these practices occurred, the punishment must be severe enough to make every healthcare institution understand that compromising patient safety will carry consequences far greater than a financial penalty. Anything less sends the wrong message.

Trust, once broken, is extraordinarily difficult to rebuild.

Sri Lankans deserve a healthcare system where every diagnosis is accurate, every medicine is safe, every laboratory meets the highest professional standards, and every patient can seek treatment without fearing that negligence, greed or complacency has replaced professional responsibility.

When human life is at stake, accountability must never be measured by the size of the fine, but by the certainty that those responsible face penalties severe enough to deter every future offender and restore public trust in the nation’s healthcare system.

(The  writer is a former Diplomat Ambassador Kana Kananathan, a lobbyist and a businessman, with over four decades of experience on the African continent. A long-time resident of Africa, he served as Sri Lanka’s envoy to Kenya, with concurrent accreditation to 22 African nations, and was the permanent representative to UN Habitat and UN Environmental Programme. Over the years, he has been the Elections Monitor across the continent, working closely with African governments, and has built enduring partnerships with African leaders. He also served as Economic and Investment Advisor to former President Professor Alpha Condé of the Republic of Guinea)

title: President’s timely intervention secures 10% US tariff rate, says Mahinda Samarasinghe - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror)- Strong Bilateral relations between the United States and Sri Lanka, timely action and relevant directives on the part of the President, hard work and focused negotiations by the Sri Lankan delegation has resulted in the reduction of tariff rates to 10 percent, Sri Lankan Ambassador to the United States Mahinda Samarasinghe said.

He said in a statement that Sri Lanka should not be complacent moving forward, as there are more challenges to overcome in order to sustain this positive outcome.

"Strong Bilateral relations between the US and Sri Lanka, timely action and relevant directives on the part of the President, hard work and focused negotiations by the Sri Lankan delegation, comprising Finance Secretary Harshana Suriyapperuma (leader of the delegation), Governor of the Central Bank Nandalal Weerasinghe, Trade Secretary Vimalenthirarajah, Chief Economic Advisor and BOI Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa and Ambassador of Sri Lanka to the United States Mahinda Samarasinghe and the day to day coordination, intelligence gathering, advice and building of goodwill by the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Washington DC, resulted in this favorable outcome for Sri Lanka," he said.

"As I complete my relatively long tenure as Ambassador in a few days’ time, I would like to leave behind a word of caution that we should not be complacent moving forward, as there are more challenges to overcome in order to sustain this positive outcome," Samarasinghe further said.

Samarasinghe said he is ready to offer his assistance to the President and the sovernment if requested and added that there is absolutely nothing that Sri Lankans cannot achieve if they work as a team while setting aside political agendas in the best interest of our beloved motherland.

summary:

Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror)- The debate on the no confidence motion on Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara got underway in Parliament a short while ago.

title: Sri Lanka seeks China aid for bamboo, forest management - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Environment Deputy Minister Anton Jayakody has called for international cooperation to tackle the global environmental crisis, saying no country can face environmental challenges alone.

Addressing a ministerial-level workshop on “Forest Resource Management and Green Development” under the Global Development Initiative (GDI) in China, Jayakody said countries must work together to find solutions and promote sustainable development.

The workshop, held from July 24 to 30, brings together environmental ministers, officials and experts from Sri Lanka, Egypt, Ethiopia, The Gambia, Liberia, Malaysia, Namibia and Thailand.

Thanking the Chinese Government for hosting the event, the Deputy Minister highlighted Sri Lanka’s commitment to sustainable environmental management and climate resilience.

During the meeting, Jayakody requested China’s support for three key areas — developing Sri Lanka’s bamboo industry, managing forest fires, and improving the country’s Forest College and training programmes.

The Sri Lankan delegation included Ministry of Environment officials and Director General of the Department of Forest Conservation P.S.C. Palamakumbura.

The Ministry said the discussions are expected to strengthen cooperation between Sri Lanka and China and support Sri Lanka’s green development efforts.

title: Lanka Premier League: Galle Gallants cruise to third win - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By M. Shamil Amit

Galle Gallants bounced back in style to record their third victory of the Lanka Premier League T20 tournament with a comfortable 60-run win over Jaffna Kings in the tenth match played under floodlights at the Rangiri Dambulla Stadium yesterday.

Chasing a challenging target of 194, Jaffna Kings were never able to gain control of the run chase.

They lost their first five wickets with only 50 runs on the board by the seventh over and failed to recover from the early setbacks. Dunith Wellalage offered some resistance with a fighting knock of 56, but the remaining batters failed to provide him with adequate support as Jaffna Kings were bowled out for 133 in 17.5 overs.

Tharindu Ratnayake and Eshan Malinga were the chief destroyers, claiming three wickets each, while Akif Javed, Dasun Shanaka and Vijayakanth Viyaskanth picked up one wicket apiece.

Earlier, Galle Gallants, who were put into bat, found themselves in early trouble after losing opener Sam Harper and Charith Asalanka inside the first three overs, with the score on 16.

Chris Lynn and Chamika Karunaratne then steadied the innings with a 48-run partnership for the third wicket. Lynn, in particular, batted with confidence and struck 46 off just 22 deliveries, including three boundaries and four sixes, before falling to Lizaad Williams.

Karunaratne was also dismissed by Williams soon afterwards, leaving the Gallants in a difficult position at 65 for four.

Sahan Arachchige then anchored the recovery and received valuable support from Mohammad Nawaz. The pair frustrated the Jaffna Kings bowlers with a rapid 68-run partnership from only 30 deliveries.

Arachchige reached his half-century in 30 balls, while Nawaz contributed a brisk 27 off 16 deliveries before being dismissed by Dilshan Madushanka.

Arachchige was run out from the final delivery of the innings after an impressive 63 off 36 balls, which included four boundaries and three sixes, as Galle Gallants finished on a commanding 193 for eight.

title: El Niño could alter weather patterns, bringing rains to some areas and dry spells to others - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - El Niño could lead to significant changes in weather patterns, with some areas experiencing excessive rainfall while others could face dry conditions, Meteorology Department Director General Ajith Wijemannage warned.

Addressing the media, Wijemannage said that during the peak phase of the El Niño condition, Sri Lanka could experience either higher-than-normal rainfall or drought conditions.

He said that according to the latest global forecasts, the El Niño phenomenon, which was previously in a weak phase, is gradually developing towards a moderate phase. The probability of it reaching its peak between October and December this year has increased to 81 percent.

Wijemannage cautioned that the impact of El Niño could result in extreme weather variations across the country, including heavy rainfall in certain areas and prolonged dry conditions in others.

The department had earlier predicted during a media briefing that the El Niño condition would peak between November and January next year, with a probability of 63 percent.

He said increased rainfall is expected during the last few days of this month and the first few days of next month in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts, as well as Galle and Matara areas.

Meanwhile, other parts of the country may experience dry weather conditions during the following month, along with an increase in the temperature felt by the human body.

The department expects considerable rainfall towards the end of September.

title: 21 companies under CID probe over alleged $700 Million import scam - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Roshan Thusara

Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) yesterday informed Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama that investigations are underway to establish the involvement of 21 leading companies in a large-scale racket involving the illegal transfer of foreign currency out of Sri Lanka under the guise of importing goods, in violation of the Customs Ordinance.

The CID made these submissions when the complaint regarding the alleged transfer of more than Rs. 190 billion worth of foreign currency overseas by falsely claiming to import goods was taken up before court.

The CID informed court that six companies linked to the alleged racket have so far been identified, while investigations are continuing to identify the involvement of other companies.

The Financial Crimes Investigation Division of the CID informed court that the suspect, identified as Jeffrey Mohamed, who has been remanded for allegedly transferring more than US$700 million overseas through fraudulent means, had acted as a facilitator of the racket.

When the suspect was produced before court by prison officials, the CID strongly objected to granting him bail, stating that he had failed to reveal the names of companies involved in the alleged scheme and had not provided assistance to the investigations.

Making further submissions, the CID’s Financial Crimes Investigation Division said:

“The fraud was carried out by sending foreign currency overseas while falsely claiming that goods were being imported. The racket was uncovered after examining the bank accounts of 36 companies.”

“The money had been transferred overseas on 10,156 occasions; however, there are no records with Customs regarding goods imported using those funds. Investigations are also underway to determine whether this involved undervaluing imported goods to evade government taxes.”

The CID told court that the suspect had operated the racket in an organised manner while posing as a director of an institution named “A.Y. Investment”, which was operating in the Colombo Fort area.

The investigators further informed court that a large quantity of US dollar notes worth millions of rupees was recovered from the suspect at the time of his arrest. A luxury vehicle worth over Rs. 200 million, allegedly purchased using illegally obtained funds, and a stock of gold were also taken into custody.

The CID said a special investigation has been launched to arrest a number of large-scale businessmen who allegedly used the suspect’s services to transfer dollars overseas illegally and evade taxes.

Appearing for the suspect, President’s Counsel M.A. Suhair and Attorney Asanka Perera requested that he be released on suitable bail, claiming that goods had been imported in accordance with legal procedures.

After considering the submissions, the Chief Magistrate observed that the suspect had not cooperated with the investigations. The Magistrate noted that considering attempts to conceal evidence and avoid court proceedings, it would not be possible to expect further cooperation from the suspect in such a major investigation.

Accordingly, the Magistrate rejected the bail application and ordered that the suspect be remanded until August 6.

title: CAA fines 23 private hospitals, labs Rs. 5.8m over expired medicines - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has filed cases against 23 private hospitals and medical laboratories across the country after islandwide raids uncovered the use and storage of expired medicines and diagnostic chemicals, overcharging for laboratory tests, and other practices that pose serious risks to public health.

The CAA said courts have so far imposed a total fine of Rs. 5,798,000 in the concluded cases.

The special inspections targeted private hospitals, medical laboratories and pharmacies with the objective of protecting public health and safeguarding consumer rights.

According to the Authority, investigators detected several serious irregularities during the raids, including the use and storage of expired chemicals for diagnostic and laboratory tests, the sale and use of expired medicines for patient care, charging fees exceeding the maximum prices approved by the CAA for laboratory tests, and storing expired chemicals together with non-expired chemicals without proper segregation.

Following the investigations, the CAA instituted legal proceedings against the 23 private hospitals and medical laboratories in the relevant Magistrate's Courts.

The Authority said legal action will also be initiated against other institutions currently under investigation.

The CAA added that islandwide raids and inspections will continue to curb practices that endanger public health and violate consumer rights. It urged the public to report similar irregularities by contacting the CAA hotline 1977 during office hours.

title: Private bus drivers, conductors to receive ETF membership - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colobmbo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Private bus drivers and conductors will be brought under the Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) scheme, marking a significant step toward extending social security benefits to employees engaged in non-government public transport services.

The Transport, Highways and Urban Development Ministry said an awareness programme on enrolling private bus crew members in the Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) scheme was held on July 21 at the Ministry Auditorium on the seventh floor of Sethsiripaya Phase II in Battaramulla.

The programme introduced participants to the role of the Employees' Trust Fund Board, the general and welfare benefits available to members, employer registration and contribution procedures, and the legal provisions governing membership under the Employees' Trust Fund Act No. 46 of 1980.

The initiative follows a decision by the ETF Board to extend membership to private sector employees engaged in public transport services, who were previously not covered under the scheme.

According to the Ministry, the programme is the first step in extending welfare benefits to employees in the non-government transport sector and will be implemented at both the central government and provincial council levels.

title: Ranil pushes for select committee to resolve 1.1 million pending court cases - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 24 (Daily Mirror) - Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe said he had proposed setting up a select committee to find ways and means to get rid of the backlog of cases.

"The government has claimed that the extension of the retirement age of judges is aimed at getting rid of the backlog of court cases. The Minister of Justice has said there are 1.1 million cases pending in courts. Therefore, I have told the Opposition Leader to hand over a proposal to the government calling for the setting up of a select committee to look into ways and means to resolve the large backlog of cases," Wickremesinghe told the media.
